note: Educational reference compiled from common Ayurvedic / ethnobotanical sources. Not medical advice. 'folder_aliases' are matched against the image-classifier class (folder) names.

plants.description: An aromatic rhizome widely used in Ayurveda as Rasna for inflammatory joint disorders and to support digestion and respiratory health.
plants.precautions: Large doses may cause gastric irritation.

plants.description: A leafy green rich in iron, calcium and vitamins, used traditionally to relieve constipation, cool the body and support blood health.
plants.precautions: High oxalate content; people prone to kidney stones should moderate intake.

plants.description: Leaves and bark of the jackfruit tree are used to help heal wounds and ulcers and to support blood sugar control.
plants.precautions: Latex is sticky and can irritate skin; fruit is high in natural sugars.

plants.description: One of the most valued Ayurvedic herbs; bitter neem leaves are a classic blood purifier used for skin diseases, oral hygiene and as a broad antimicrobial.
plants.precautions: Not recommended in pregnancy; seed oil is toxic if ingested in quantity, especially by children.

plants.description: A mucilaginous leafy vegetable used as a gentle laxative and a cooling, nutritive green rich in iron and vitamins A and C.
plants.precautions: High in oxalates; moderate if prone to kidney stones.

plants.description: Mustard leaves and seeds are warming and stimulant; seed paste and oil are applied externally for pain and used to loosen chest congestion.
plants.precautions: Seed paste can blister sensitive skin if left on too long.

plants.description: A thorny shrub whose tart vitamin-C-rich berries and leaves are used for fever, digestive complaints and as an astringent.
plants.precautions: Unripe fruit is very sour and astringent; latex can irritate.

plants.description: Lemon juice and leaves are rich in vitamin C and citric acid, used to aid digestion, soothe sore throats and as a refreshing antimicrobial.
plants.precautions: Acidic; can erode tooth enamel and aggravate acid reflux in excess.

plants.description: A large-leaved fig whose bark and fruit are used as astringents for diarrhea and to support wound healing.
plants.precautions: Latex may irritate sensitive skin.

plants.description: The sacred peepal tree's bark and leaves are used for respiratory complaints, skin disorders and to support blood sugar control.
plants.precautions: Generally well tolerated; consult a practitioner for therapeutic doses.

plants.description: Hibiscus flowers and leaves are a classic hair tonic and cooling agent, also used to support healthy menstruation and blood pressure.
plants.precautions: May lower blood pressure; caution if hypotensive or pregnant.

plants.description: Fragrant jasmine flowers and leaves are used as a mild sedative, to soothe the mind and as an antiseptic for mouth ulcers and skin.
plants.precautions: Strong fragrance may trigger headache in sensitive individuals.

plants.description: Mango leaves and bark are astringent and are traditionally used to support blood sugar control and to treat diarrhea and gum problems.
plants.precautions: Sap and unripe fruit can irritate; diabetic use should be monitored.

plants.description: Cooling mint leaves are a well-known digestive and carminative, relieving gas, nausea and congestion.
plants.precautions: Concentrated menthol oil should not be applied near the face of infants.

plants.description: A nutrient-dense superfood tree; moringa leaves are rich in protein, iron and vitamins and are used to combat malnutrition, inflammation and high blood sugar.
plants.precautions: Root and bark contain alkaloids and should be avoided in pregnancy.

plants.description: The leaves of this fast-growing cherry tree are brewed as an antioxidant tea used for headache, fever and to support blood pressure and sugar levels.
plants.precautions: Limited clinical data; use traditionally and in moderation.

plants.description: Aromatic curry leaves aid digestion, support blood sugar and cholesterol balance, and are a traditional remedy for hair health.
plants.precautions: Generally safe as food; concentrated extracts should be used cautiously.

uses: external skin diseases (classical, purified preparations only)
plants.description: Karavira is a HIGHLY POISONOUS ornamental shrub. In classical Ayurveda only specially purified (shodhana) preparations are used externally; all parts are cardiotoxic.
plants.precautions: TOXIC / POISONOUS. Do not ingest any part. Even small amounts can cause fatal heart arrhythmia. Listed here only for identification and safety awareness.

plants.description: Parijata leaf juice is a renowned traditional remedy for stubborn fevers, sciatica and arthritis.
plants.precautions: Very bitter; large doses may cause nausea.

plants.description: The 'Queen of Herbs' in Ayurveda; Tulsi is a revered adaptogen used for coughs, colds, respiratory infections, stress relief and immune support.
plants.precautions: May have a mild blood-thinning and blood-sugar-lowering effect; caution with anticoagulants and before surgery.

plants.description: Aromatic betel leaves are warming and antiseptic, used to relieve congestion, aid digestion and dress wounds.
plants.precautions: Habitual chewing with areca nut and tobacco is strongly linked to oral cancer; the leaf alone is the medicinal part.

plants.description: Thick aromatic leaves used as a household remedy for cough, cold and congestion in children and adults, and to aid digestion.
plants.precautions: Generally safe in culinary amounts; concentrated use should be moderated.

plants.description: Karanja seed oil and leaves are a classic Ayurvedic remedy for skin diseases, wounds and parasitic infections.
plants.precautions: Seed oil is for external use; internal use only under guidance.

plants.description: Guava leaves are a widely used remedy for diarrhea, oral health and to support blood sugar control, owing to their astringent tannins.
plants.precautions: Excess leaf decoction may cause constipation.

plants.description: Dadima is highly esteemed in Ayurveda; the fruit, rind and bark are used for digestion, diarrhea, intestinal worms and heart health.
plants.precautions: Bark contains alkaloids and is used for worms only under supervision.

uses: to cool the body and reduce burning sensation
plants.description: Cooling sandalwood paste and oil are classic Ayurvedic remedies for skin inflammation, prickly heat, urinary burning and mental calm.
plants.precautions: Pure essential oil should be diluted; avoid internal use of oil without guidance.

plants.description: Jamun is one of Ayurveda's best-known herbs for blood sugar control; the seed powder, fruit and bark are astringent and antidiabetic.
plants.precautions: May lower blood sugar; monitor when combined with diabetes medication.

plants.description: Rose apple leaves and bark are astringent and antimicrobial, used for diarrhea, fever and to support blood sugar control.
plants.precautions: Seeds may contain trace cyanogenic compounds; do not consume in quantity.

plants.description: An ornamental shrub whose root and milky latex are used traditionally for toothache, eye complaints and skin problems.
plants.precautions: Latex can irritate; root contains alkaloids — internal use only under guidance.

plants.description: Fenugreek leaves and seeds are a classic remedy for blood sugar and cholesterol control, to boost lactation and aid digestion.
plants.precautions: Can lower blood sugar; high doses are not advised in pregnancy as they may stimulate the uterus.
